transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining this medication-safety huddle. As we prepare for the medication safety review this afternoon before the new intravenous anticoagulant protocol goes live on the night shift, I need to hear from each of you on any operational findings related to the protocol. Pharmacy, let's start with you — what are you seeing in terms of stocking in the automated dispensing cabinets and any issues with the electronic medication record ordering? I'll also need reports from laboratory medicine, nursing education, and clinical information technology before I make my final decision on any temporary safety safeguards.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to report a significant safety concern. Since Monday, I've verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations. To mitigate this risk, pharmacy can remove the bedside stock from the automated dispensing cabinets and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to report a laboratory medicine finding. Our anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the laboratory's approved replacement for monitoring patients on this protocol is an aPTT test every six hours.
transcript.speaker: A3
transcript.raw_output: {"type": "reveal", "fact_id": "PF2", "text": "I need to report a laboratory medicine finding. Our anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the laboratory's approved replacement for monitoring patients on this protocol is an aPTT test every six hours."}

transcript.text: I need to report a nursing education finding. My competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight's shift have not completed the new anticoagulant administration module. Each of these nurses must receive charge-nurse sign-off before they are permitted to administer this medication.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a clinical information technology finding to report. I've confirmed that a high-priority electronic medication-record alert can be deployed at 16:00 today. This alert will warn clinicians about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before the order can be released, which directly addresses the selection errors pharmacy has already identified.
transcript.speaker: A5

decisions.safety_protocol: Temporary hold on bedside stock of anticoagulant in automated dispensing cabinets; supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during the temporary period.
decisions.dispensing_concentration: 1 mg/mL pharmacy-prepared syringes only; remove both 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL bedside stock from automated dispensing cabinets to eliminate selection errors.
decisions.laboratory_monitoring: aPTT test every six hours as the laboratory's approved replacement for anti-Xa monitoring until the analyzer is calibrated on Friday at 17:00.
decisions.nurse_authorization: Charge-nurse sign-off required for all 18 nurses who have not completed the anticoagulant administration module before they are permitted to administer this medication.
decisions.electronic_alert: Deploy the high-priority electronic medication-record alert at 16:00 today to warn clinicians about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before order release.

commitments.detail: Remove bedside stock of both anticoagulant concentrations from automated dispensing cabinets and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during the temporary hold.
Use aPTT testing every six hours as the approved replacement for anti-Xa monitoring until analyzer calibration is complete on Friday at 17:00.
Ensure charge-nurse sign-off for each of the 18 nurses who have not completed the administration module before they administer this medication tonight.
Deploy the high-priority concentration-selection alert at 16:00 today with mandatory acknowledgment before order release.
